chief_complaint: Persistent cough and shortness of breath, worse with exertion.

medications_prescribed.name: Albuterol Inhaler
medications_prescribed.frequency: Every 4-6 hours as needed for shortness of breath

doctor_notes: Patient presents with an acute exacerbation of her known COPD. Symptoms have worsened over the past 3 days, with increased cough, sputum production, and dyspnea. Vital signs show mild hypertension. WBC count is elevated, suggesting an infectious component. ABG shows mild hypoxemia with normal pH and pCO2. Treatment initiated with systemic corticosteroids and bronchodilator therapy. Advised on adherence to medication and breathing exercises. Follow-up appointment scheduled.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: Hello Eleanor, tell me what's been bothering you.

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: Doctor, I've been having this cough for days now, and it's hard to catch my breath, especially when I walk to the kitchen. My chest feels tight.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: I see. Have you noticed any changes in your phlegm? Is it thicker or a different color?

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: Yes, it's gotten a bit more yellow, and there's more of it than usual.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: Okay, we'll do some tests to see what's going on. I'm going to prescribe a short course of steroids to help with the inflammation and your breathing. Please take your inhaler regularly.

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: Thank you, Doctor. I'll do my best.

follow_up_actions: Return to clinic in 1 week for follow-up.
